narrative_purpose: The chapter's representative cover: a single image that reads as 'time on this world is told by light, not by a moving sky', making a reader want to open a chapter about the rhythm of Pandoran days and eclipses.
subject: A vast banded gas giant hanging fixed and high in the sky, its great oval eye-storm turned toward the viewer, partly catching a thin bright rim of light along one limb. Low and off to one side, a small fierce yellow-white sun-star sits close to the planet's edge, about to slip behind it, throwing long amber shadows across the land. In the lower foreground, a dark ridge of glowing blue-green alien forest and one tiny distant slender figure standing still, looking up.
scene: Late afternoon on an alien moon at the hour the locals call 'eclipse' - the sun about to vanish behind the giant planet. The light is going long and amber, beginning to thin toward twilight. Faint companion moons hang in the distance.
camera: Wide cinematic establishing shot, slightly low angle looking up past the ridge so the motionless planet towers over the scene and the small sun reads as the thing that moves.
light: Warm low amber key from the sinking sun-star raking across the ridge, cool indigo twilight gathering in the sky, bioluminescent teal-cyan glow rising from the forest below; a thin warm rim along the planet's limb.
palette: Deep void-indigo sky, warm amber low light along the land, teal and cyan forest glow, cream-and-rust planet bands, a scarce bright gold point for the sun.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, strong atmospheric depth.
detail_level: Crisp on the near ridge and glowing forest; the giant planet softer and atmospheric; the sun a clean bright point; distant moons dissolving into haze.
composition: Giant planet anchored upper-left filling much of the sky, small sun near its lower-right limb on a third line, ridge and tiny figure along the lower third for scale - the eye reads the fixed planet against the about-to-set sun.
consistency_notes: This banded gas giant (cream/rust/grey bands, one large eye-storm) is Polyphemus and must look identical wherever it appears in this chapter and consistent with the where-is-pandora chapter. Cool Pandora palette, bioluminescent key glow from below.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no clock imagery, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no oversaturation, no cartoon or anime style
